onboarding.metaTitle: Express interest in coaching — Fareed Quraishi
onboarding.metaDescription: Send a short message about life coaching. Name, email, which pilot option interests you, and — if you want — a sentence about what you would like to be different. Nothing is booked or charged by sending it.

intro.title: Let’s explore working together.
intro.lede: This begins a conversation: about what you are interested in, how I work, and whether we would be a good fit to work together. It asks for your name, an email address, which option interests you, and — if you want — a sentence or two about what you would like to be different.
intro.note: Nothing is booked, charged, or reserved by sending this — and it does not commit you to beginning.

reassure.title: What this is, and what it is not
paragraphs: This is not a clinical intake. I do not need your history, a diagnosis, or an account of the hardest thing that has happened to you in order to reply to a message. If we end up working together, we will get to know each other at a pace you set, in conversation.

You do not need to know which option you want, or what you want to work on, or how to describe it. Many people arrive with a sentence along the lines of: something is not working and I cannot quite say what. That is a perfectly good place to begin.

You also do not need to have decided anything. Expressing interest is not a purchase, it does not reserve one of the pilot places, and it does not guarantee a start date. It starts a conversation, which you can end at any point without explanation.

form.title: Your details
form.lede: Please share only what you are comfortable putting in an ordinary email.

interest.label: What are you interested in?
interest.hint: Pick the closest option. It is not a commitment, and you can change your mind.

unsure.label: I’m not sure yet
unsure.note: That is a normal place to start.

message.label: What would you like to be different in your life as a result of coaching?
message.hint: Optional. A sentence or two is plenty. No history, no diagnosis, and nothing you would rather say in person.

consent.label: I have read and understand the scope of this work
consent.text: Coaching is personal development support. It is not psychotherapy, diagnosis, medical treatment, or crisis support, and it does not replace them. I agree that Fareed may reply to the email address I have given, and I understand that sending this message books no session, reserves no place, and takes no payment.

form.privacyNote: Please do not include medical, diagnostic, or psychiatric information. This form is not monitored for urgent or crisis support. If you need immediate help, contact a crisis line or emergency services.
form.success: Thank you — your message has reached me. Nothing has been scheduled or charged, and no place has been reserved. I aim to respond personally within three business days at the address you gave, and I will tell you honestly whether I think coaching is a good fit and what the next step might be. If you do not hear back, check your spam folder and then email me directly.
form.noscript: This form needs JavaScript to send. If you would rather write directly — or the form does not work — email me at

how.title: What happens after you send this

steps.name: It comes to me
steps.body: Straight to my inbox. No assistant, no automated sequence, no mailing list.

steps.name: I reply personally
steps.body: I aim to respond within three business days, saying whether I think the work is a fit and what I would suggest next.

steps.name: We work out the next step
steps.body: That may be a short exchange by email, a paid session, or a referral elsewhere if that is more appropriate. It depends on your situation and on what I can offer at the time.

steps.name: You decide
steps.body: If we go ahead, the practical terms are sent in writing before anything is paid. If it is not a fit, that is a normal and acceptable outcome.
